outcomes: Finds the perpetual check for the side that is worse in a mixed set of positions
Lists the king's escape squares and the blocks and captures before relying on the checks
Says which feature of a position stops a series of checks from repeating
sources: items IBds35-16..19 (authored, content/items/lesson-ds35.json; edits of the position of Lichess puzzle Iomgk, CC0), IL-VscmF, IL-NfdoP, IL-3AdsD (Lichess puzzle database, CC0)
lesson L-TAC-PERPETUAL-1 (the idea and the find-the-perpetual step are taught there)

steps.text:
This lesson follows **Perpetual check: the draw you can force**, where you were told to find the perpetual. Now nobody tells you. You are the side that is behind, and you must look for the checks yourself.
A row of checks is not yet a perpetual. It becomes one only if the king cannot leave the checks, nothing can block or capture the checking piece, and the position repeats.

**Test before you rely on it.** (1) List your checking moves. (2) For each one, count the king's squares and ask whether anything can block or capture the checker. (3) Find your next check: is its square guarded? Only if every answer leaves you another check do the checks repeat.
**Rule of thumb:** a king boxed in by its own pawns is the usual sign; a guard of the checking square breaks it.

steps.title: Same checks, one change
steps.prompt: White is behind in material in all three. Same first check, one change each time. Predict, then check.
In the silent positions, which check did you test first, and which escape square, block or capture did you look for before you trusted the sequence? Write it on paper before you move.
